author: xiaokuerz
title: fix(audio): reset stale fade state when GainNode is reused/reconnected

questions.prompt: ResetFadeState() sets fadeInState_ = true but collFadeInState_ = false. Why the asymmetry? What would go wrong if collFadeInState_ were also set to true?

options.text: fadeInState_ controls per-stream fade-in (desired on reconnect to avoid pop), while collFadeInState_ controls collaborative fade-in — a separate mechanism that should not be triggered on reconnect; setting it to true would start an unwanted collaborative fade-in cycle
It is a typo — both should be true to ensure fade-in on reconnect
collFadeInState_ must be false because the collaborative fade-in counter is managed externally and setting it to true would leak state
fadeInState_ and collFadeInState_ control the same fade-in but at different sample rates, so both being true would cause double fade-in amplification

questions.explanation: fadeInState_ and collFadeInState_ are two independent fade mechanisms: per-stream and collaborative. On reconnect, you want per-stream fade-in to avoid a pop, but you do NOT want to trigger collaborative fade-in (which is managed separately). Setting collFadeInState_ = true would incorrectly start a collaborative fade-in cycle on a node that just needs its stale state cleared.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the asymmetry is intentional: per-stream fade-in is wanted on reconnect, collaborative fade-in is not.

questions.prompt: Suppose a GainNode is in the middle of an active fade-out (fadeOutState_ = FADING_FADEOUT, not DONE_FADEOUT) when CreateGainNode is called for a session that already has a node. What does calling ResetFadeState() do to the in-progress fade-out?

options.text: It completes the fade-out first, then resets the state — the node goes silent before fade-in begins
It aborts the in-progress fade-out: fadeOutState_ becomes NO_FADEOUT, fadeProcessedBytes_ is zeroed, and fadeInState_ is set to true — the node transitions directly to fade-in
It throws an error because FADING_FADEOUT is not a stale state and ResetFadeState only handles DONE_FADEOUT
It leaves fadeOutState_ unchanged and only resets the collaborative fade fields

questions.explanation: ResetFadeState() unconditionally sets fadeOutState_ = NO_FADEOUT and fadeProcessedBytes_ = 0, regardless of the current state. It does not check whether the state is stale vs active — it always clears everything. So a FADING_FADEOUT would be aborted mid-flight, and the node would immediately start fading in.
questions.reinforce: Correct — ResetFadeState is unconditional; it does not distinguish stale from active fade states.

questions.prompt: The ResetFadeState_PreventsSilenceOnReusedNode test sets nodeInfo.fadeType = DEFAULT_FADE, but the other test (ResetFadeState_ClearsStaleDoneFadeout) does NOT set fadeType. Why does this test need DEFAULT_FADE?

options.text: DEFAULT_FADE enables the fade processing code path in SignalProcess; without it, SignalProcess may skip fade logic entirely, so DONE_FADEOUT would not actually silence frames — the state-clearing test does not need it because it checks member variables directly, not through SignalProcess
DEFAULT_FADE is required to construct a valid HpaeGainNode; the state-clearing test works only because it manually sets fadeOutState_ after construction
It is a copy-paste inconsistency — both tests should have the same fadeType
DEFAULT_FADE sets the fade duration in bytes; without it, the fade completes instantly and the test cannot distinguish before/after behavior

questions.explanation: The state-clearing test only verifies that ResetFadeState() sets the right member variable values — it never calls SignalProcess, so fadeType is irrelevant. The silence-prevention test calls SignalProcess and checks actual audio output, which requires the fade processing path to be active. DEFAULT_FADE enables that path; without it, SignalProcess might not consult fadeOutState_ at all, and the test would not demonstrate the silence bug.
questions.reinforce: Correct — DEFAULT_FADE gates the fade code path in SignalProcess; the state-only test does not need it.

questions.prompt: If you removed the ResetFadeState() call but kept ResetVolume(), what would happen to a reused GainNode that had fadeOutState_ = DONE_FADEOUT from a previous Pause?

options.text: ResetVolume() also clears fade state, so removing ResetFadeState() has no effect
The node would remain permanently muted because ResetVolume() does not touch fadeOutState_; DONE_FADEOUT makes SignalProcess silence every frame regardless of the volume value
The node would play normally because ResetVolume() restores the gain, overriding the silencing effect of DONE_FADEOUT
The node would play at reduced volume but not be fully muted, since ResetVolume partially counteracts the fade state

questions.explanation: The comment in ResetFadeState explains: DONE_FADEOUT makes SignalProcess silence every frame. This silencing is a state-driven action in SignalProcess, not a volume multiplier. ResetVolume() sets the volume-related fields (curGain_, curSystemGain_) but does not touch fadeOutState_. So even after ResetVolume(), SignalProcess would see DONE_FADEOUT and zero out every frame, keeping the node muted.
questions.reinforce: Correct — DONE_FADEOUT silences in SignalProcess independently of volume; ResetVolume cannot fix it.

questions.prompt: The test sets fadeProcessedBytes_ = 100 and collFadeProcessedBytes_ = 200 as stale values. After ResetFadeState(), both are verified to be 0. What is the purpose of zeroing these counters? What would happen if they were left at their stale values?

options.text: fadeProcessedBytes_ tracks how many bytes have been processed in the current fade cycle; without resetting it, the fade-in logic would think it is already partway through the ramp and skip the beginning, causing an abrupt gain jump instead of a smooth fade-in
fadeProcessedBytes_ is a memory allocation counter; without resetting it, the node would leak memory proportional to the stale value
fadeProcessedBytes_ stores the target fade duration in bytes; without resetting it, the fade has a different duration
fadeProcessedBytes_ is only used for logging and metrics; zeroing it has no functional effect on audio output

questions.explanation: fadeProcessedBytes_ is a progress counter for the current fade cycle. If it retains a stale value (e.g. 100 from a previous fade-out), the fade-in logic would calculate its ramp position from byte 100 instead of 0, effectively skipping the first portion of the fade-in ramp. This would cause an abrupt gain change (a pop) rather than a smooth ramp from the starting gain to the target.
questions.reinforce: Correct — stale progress bytes would skip the start of the fade-in ramp, causing a pop.

questions.prompt: Both ConnectInputCluster (in renderer_manager, line 764) and CreateGainNode (here in process_cluster, line 162) can call ResetFadeState() on a reused GainNode during a reconnect. If both execute for the same session, is calling ResetFadeState() twice a problem?

options.text: It is safe — ResetFadeState() is idempotent: it unconditionally assigns the same values (NO_FADEOUT, true/false, 0), so the second call overwrites with identical values and has no side effect beyond an extra log line
The second call would throw because fadeOutState_ is already NO_FADEOUT and the function expects a non-reset state
The second call would toggle fadeInState_ back to false, muting the node
The second call would cause fadeProcessedBytes_ to underflow because it is already 0

questions.explanation: ResetFadeState() only contains unconditional assignments (no reads, no branches, no assertions). Calling it twice sets fadeOutState_ = NO_FADEOUT, fadeInState_ = true, fadeProcessedBytes_ = 0, etc. — all the same values the first call already set. There are no side effects beyond field assignments and a log line. The function is idempotent by construction.
questions.reinforce: Correct — unconditional assignments make ResetFadeState idempotent; double-calls are safe.
